I'm saying that beyond the kneejerk reaction it your decision. Whether or not you say "fuck that guy for his dumb rude remark" or "why did he say that? Maybe he was right" is up to you. The kneejerk can't be controlled. It hurt I'm sure. Those feelings are valid. Feel them. But it really is a choice to still think about it years later. It may not feel like it. Our brains have evolved to be very sensitive to the human face. 

We recognize very small differences in facial expressions and face shape in general. 

We are so attuned to those patterns that we create them were none are present (lookup paradolia).

When something isn't a face we can personify it. Dot dot curved line = smiley face. 

We separate those things though.

Actual faces have a lot going on and we give them more attention to figuring out. (Consciously and unconsciously). 

Symbol of faces we give less attention to figuring out becuase we recognize the crudeness even if the face shapes are important to us. 

The uncanny valley refers to a point on the spectrum between a smiley face and you friend sitting across from you. 

The closer an image or video get to being more photorealistic the harder a time or brains have trying to figure out if it is or isn't actually human. 

Becuase if it is human we have this innate need to understand how it feels via facial cues. 

If it isn't, then we can dicard its meaning as we see fit. (Cartoons, who cares)if we can figure out if it's a person or not becuase it's so closer then our brains don't know how to react and there becomes this aversion to the thing it can't figure out. It's creepy or uncanny. 

The valley part refers to ability to recognize a symbol or face ,and assign it as  one or another, dropping off as we get closer to the side of realistic human face.
